title: Who is responsible when the AI is wrong? Why legal duty does not equal technical visibility
headline: The gap between legal responsibility and technical visibility in AI systems
summary: When AI-assisted decisions are challenged, organizations face a disconnect between who holds legal duty and who possesses the technical evidence to reconstruct how a decision was made. Because AI outcomes emerge from complex supply chains involving multiple vendors, models, and data sources, critical configuration and version records are often missing.
why_it_matters: Organizations deploying AI must implement robust vendor management and logging practices to capture model versions, prompts, and configurations, otherwise they cannot meet their accountability obligations when outcomes are contested.

quotes.text: The organization that must explain a decision often does not hold the evidence it needs to do so.
Without version records and change logs, it can be impossible to say which configuration produced a contested outcome.

classification.significance_reason: Highlights a critical operational and governance challenge regarding accountability and auditability in complex AI supply chains.
